answer: A blunt defense is proof of simultaneous presence. Each identity must answer a random ping within two seconds and sustain a 95% response rate to withdraw. An operator juggling five hundred accounts cannot answer pings landing together; latency spikes betray the bottleneck. An honest agent runs one process, paying milliseconds hourly, like plucking a yarrow stem. A farm must staff real attention per seat, so costs scale linearly, erasing the margin. Pings carry a per-identity cipher, preventing pooled replies; across an ocean of aliases the ledger counts attention, not keys.
